parole.significato: [sometimes angry] annoyance, vexation, indignation, anger, worry
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish harm (ultimately from Proto-Germanic *harmaz (“harm; shame; pain”) whence also Estonian härm).

parole.significato: beam, balk, girder (long piece of timber, metal or concrete used in construction as horizontal support)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish balk, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *balkô.

parole.significato: cardamom bread, pulla (mildly sweet, leavened baked good made of wheat and flavored with crushed cardamom, resembling v…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish bulle, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *bullǭ. Doublet of pullo.

parole.significato: to be fine, to be okay, to get along, to cope
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish bärga (“to protect, to manage”), from Proto-Germanic *berganą. Long considered colloquial or informal, but has become widespread in all contexts by the 21st century at the latest.
Borrowed from Swedish salva, from Proto-Germanic *salbō.

parole.significato: soft soap, potassium soap (gel-like soap obtained by cooking potassium hydroxide with natural oils and fats)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Swedish såpa (“soft soap”), from Proto-Germanic *saipǭ (“soap”). Doublet of saippua and soopa.
Borrowed from Swedish stall, ultimately from Proto-Germanic *stallaz.
